part.text:
The file on disk now passes `validate` (OK) and `parse`. The deeper `inspect` check reports only two items left — both feature-gated. Here's what was wrong and what I changed.

## Why it failed to validate (the parse errors)

1. **Line 3 — unquoted description.** `person "Driver" Arrives at and departs from the garage.` — the description had to be a quoted string literal. Fixed to `"Arrives at and departs from the garage."`
2. **Line 6 — duplicate identifier.** The second container was also named `entry`, colliding with the first. It was meant to be `exit` (line 10 referenced `exit -> billing`, but `exit` was never defined). Renamed it to `exit`.
3. **Line 11 — use before definition.** `billing -> traffic` referenced `traffic`, but `traffic` wasn't defined until line 13. Moved the `traffic` element up so it's defined before any relationship uses it.

## Additional fixes (from the deeper `inspect` check)

4. **No workspace scope** → added `configuration { scope "SoftwareSystem" }`.
5. **`driver -> entry` missing a technology** → added `"Physical"` (the promoted person→system relationship inherits it, clearing both technology errors).
6. **Containers not on any view** → added a `container garage "GarageContainers"` view.

Nothing was removed — all people, systems, containers, and relationships are preserved.

## One thing I couldn't fix from the file

`inspect` still flags two items: the software system is "missing documentation" and "missing decisions." Those require the `!docs` / `!decisions` directives, which are gated behind features (`structurizr.feature.dsl.documentation`, etc.) that aren't enabled in this environment — I tried enabling them via `properties` and `configuration { properties }` and they're not permitted from within the DSL. If you enable those features on the server side, you can add the documentation/decisions blocks and those two will clear.

The workspace itself now validates cleanly.
